mechanism_narrative: The two-week rise in RETAIL_REC from -72.0 to -64.6 is a persistent recovery signal: retail footfall momentum carries into the next four weeks because consumers gradually resume non-essential trips.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -72.0 at t-2w to -64.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the t-2w to t-0w rise.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility is the access channel for retail and recreation. When TRANSIT rises above -60 and holds, it signals restored intra-city movement that lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -60 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -64.3 at t-2w to -59.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is lower than last 28-day mean while TRANSIT has remained above -60 for the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility above baseline is the clearest stay-at-home signal. As RESIDENTIAL declines from 20.0 to 17.4, households reallocate time to non-residential activities, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18.0 for one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 20.0 at t-2w to 17.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 14-day mean is lower than last 14-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains below 18.0.

mechanism_narrative: Policy easing is revealed jointly by WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovering. When both remain above their t-2w levels, reopening permits retail activity to expand over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES > -55 and TRANSIT > -61 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -54.6 at t-2w to -53.1 at t-0w; TRANSIT rose from -64.3 to -59.1
failure_condition: Next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than last 28-day mean when WORKPLACES > -55 and TRANSIT > -61 jointly hold.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-February to mid-March seasonal transition increases daylight and outdoor activity, raising PARKS and spilling into RETAIL_REC. This spring ramp should lift retail mobility over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -63.7 at t-2w to -58.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not higher than last 28-day mean despite PARKS rising in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 18.5 while GROCERY_PHARM falls below -35, it signals renewed stay-at-home behavior and essential-trip retrenchment; retail-recreation declines over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 18.5 and GROCERY_PHARM falls below -35 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 17.4 and GROCERY_PHARM was -31.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Next 14-day mean RETAIL_REC is higher than last 14-day mean when RESIDENTIAL > 18.5 and GROCERY_PHARM < -35 jointly occur.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery is fragile and dependent on transit access. If TRANSIT falls back below -62 within one week, consumers lose mobility capacity and RETAIL_REC declines over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -62 for one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -59.1 at t-0w after rising from -64.3 at t-2w
failure_condition: Next 7-day mean RETAIL_REC is higher than last 7-day mean while TRANSIT falls below -62.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility reflects essential-trip willingness. When GROCERY_PHARM rises above -30, it signals broader consumer confidence and precedes RETAIL_REC recovery over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -30 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -39.4 at t-2w to -31.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Next 14-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than last 14-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM has remained above -30 for two weeks.
